wall_justification:
7,200 s (2 h) of wall-clock per sample.  Justification: 5 concurrent
workers is what the measured footprint (about 10 GiB resident per worker, still
rising) allows on this shared machine, and 29 samples x 2 h / 5 workers is
about 11.6 h - the largest per-sample wall that keeps the whole collection
inside a single day of the stage's 40-core budget.  Every run in flight had
reached or passed that wall when it was stopped.

configuration.invocation: decodiphy -t tree.nwk -d distances.txt -o OUTDIR (documented defaults: --method hill, --quick 1, --radius 2, --seed 1142, --fix_k 0, --optimizer osqp, --min_p 0.01)
configuration.concurrency: 1 (pilot) and 5 (batch), chosen from the measured resident set size on a shared 62-core machine with other users' jobs running
configuration.memory_limit: RLIMIT_AS 60 GB (pilot) and 30 GB (batch); neither was reached

measured_input_stage.note: treeswift's leaf-to-leaf distance matrix alone materialises 111.8 million entries; the enclosing get_input_matrices had not returned after 63 minutes when the probe was stopped

pruning.note: unlike the krepp ANI cases, every backbone leaf carries a distance here, so the input stage keeps the full panel

what_this_is_not: This is the cost of this stage's invocation on this machine, not a property of DecoDiPhy: the parent publication ran it on this same collection.  Its README documents --warm_start because the search "can be time extensive", i.e. for inputs of this size the intended workflow resumes a search across runs instead of driving one run to the low-abundance stop. No conclusion about the tool's behaviour on these samples is drawn here.
what_is_reported_instead: Theta_1 and Lambda_1 for all 29 samples, which need no DecoDiPhy run: Theta_1 is imported from stage 298 and Lambda_1 was computed here in 1.1 s per sample.
